transport.invocation_template: python queue_client.py --role producer --producer claude --method GET|POST --path <allowed path>
transport.authentication: local-ip-and-producer-token; claude producer key read from private/credentials.json (never printed)
notes: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 is required in Git Bash or /health/consumers is rewritten as a Windows path.
The server is single-threaded. /tasks and /tasks/pending can take 13-36 s with 100 stored tasks; short client timeouts (15 s) time out even when the server is healthy.
/health/consumers, /tasks/<id>/status and /tasks/<id> respond in under 1 s when the server is not busy.

canaries.interpretation: The transport delivered the task and Muse independently claimed and rejected it. The rejection is a platform safety boundary, not a transport failure. The canary text contained credential-related words that triggered the check.

canaries.note: Simplified read-only canary without credential wording; result to be appended when claimed.

gate_implications.statement: A real, independent Muse channel exists and is reachable. No gate may be marked VERIFIED until Muse returns a verdict JSON on the same commit. Claude's own tests are always labelled self-test.
gate_implications.reliability_risk: Queue latency and occasional non-response require retries and generous timeouts; a timeout is recorded as a transport observation, not as a Muse verdict.
